subject: Mathematics
central_question: How do ordered pairs build relations, and what extra condition turns a relation into a function?
in_scope_units: Cartesian products of sets, ordered pairs, counting, and ordered triplets.
Relations as subsets of Cartesian products, with domain, range, codomain, and representations.
Functions as relations assigning one and only one image to each input.
Identity, constant, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, and greatest integer functions and graphs.
Algebra of real functions: sum, difference, scalar multiple, product, and quotient.
banned_topics: Composition and inverse functions, which are not developed in this chapter.
Equivalence-relation classification beyond the miscellaneous examples.

known_pitfalls.correction: Order matters, so the two products are generally unequal.

known_pitfalls.claim: Range and codomain are always equal.
known_pitfalls.correction: The range consists only of actual images and is a subset of the codomain.
A function must assign every input exactly one image.

known_pitfalls.claim: Different inputs cannot share an output.
known_pitfalls.correction: Different inputs may have the same image in a function.

known_pitfalls.claim: f/g is defined on the whole common domain.
known_pitfalls.correction: Points where g(x)=0 must also be excluded.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Example 1 for equality of ordered pairs.
NCERT Example 7 for domain, codomain, and range of a relation.
NCERT Example 11 for the function test.
NCERT Examples 13 and 15 for graphs, domains, and ranges.
NCERT Example 16 for algebra of real functions.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 2.
